questions.question: What does Spring Boot DevTools do when your compiled classes change?
options: Rebuilds the JAR file
Restarts the running application automatically
Deploys the app to a server
Deletes the target folder
questions.explanation: DevTools watches target/classes and restarts the application context when compiled classes change.

questions.question: Why is a DevTools restart much faster than a cold start?
options: It skips starting the web server
It caches every HTTP response
It keeps libraries in a base class loader and reloads only your own classes
It runs the app on a faster JVM
questions.explanation: Only the restart class loader holding your classes is rebuilt; the heavy libraries stay loaded.

questions.question: An app runs with ./mvnw spring-boot:run and DevTools. You change the reply from "4 free slots" to "3 free slots" and compile, without stopping the app. What does the next request return?
options: The reply with 3 free slots
The reply with 4 free slots, until you stop and start the app
An error, because the class changed while running
Both replies, one after the other
questions.explanation: Compiling changes target/classes, DevTools restarts the app, and the new code answers the next request.

questions.question: A student adds DevTools and saves a controller change, but the app never restarts. What is the most likely cause?
options: DevTools only works with Gradle
The port must be changed after each edit
DevTools needs the Actuator starter
The change was saved but not compiled, so target/classes did not change
questions.explanation: DevTools reacts to compiled classes; switch on automatic build in the IDE or run ./mvnw compile.

questions.question: During development an error response showed a message and a stack trace. In production, run with java -jar, the same error shows only the status and error name. Why?
options: Production servers delete stack traces from Java
DevTools added those details in development, and it is not included in the packaged JAR
java -jar runs an older version of Spring Boot
The error only happens in development
questions.explanation: DevTools turns on detailed error responses while developing; the packaged JAR leaves DevTools out.
